extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders and members of the public submitting comments on ACF proposed rules (child welfare advocates, state agencies, providers, tribal representatives, caregivers, foster youth)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments on proposed rules issued by the Administration for Children and Families (ACF), with specific recommendations for child welfare, foster care, adoption, child care, and refugee resettlement rulemakings. Covers procedural steps (where/how to submit, deadlines) and substantive evidence/authority to include in effective comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find the Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Children's Bureau maintains a page containing both regulations and notices for public comment at acf.gov/cb/laws-policies/federal-laws/regulatory-actions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate the specific NPRM or notice on the Children's Bureau regulatory actions page to ensure you are commenting on the correct docket and to find links to the official materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Regulations.gov and include plain-language summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The docket on https://www.regulations.gov will include a plain language summary of the NPRM as required by 5 U.S.C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit comments via Regulations.gov; consult the plain-language summary provided there (statutory requirement) to align your comment with the rule's stated purposes and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow comment deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rules are typically open for a 60-day public comment period
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note and adhere to the deadline for each NPRM (often 60 days). Late comments may not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to ACF's specifically requested areas for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: While ACF welcomes comment on any topic related to the proposed rule, there are often key areas within the NPRM where ACF is specifically requesting input from commenters
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and prioritize addressing the specific questions or topic areas called out in the NPRM; targeted responses to those prompts are especially useful to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify experience with affected populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify experience with affected populations (foster youth, providers, caregivers)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State your role and direct experience (e.g., foster youth, state agency staff, provider, caregiver) so reviewers can assess the perspective and weight of your comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific authorizing statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific Title IV-B/IV-E, CCDF, or other authorizing statutes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference the statutory authority relevant to the rule to ground comments in the legal framework governing the program; specify relevant sections when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference major child welfare statutes (ASFA, MEPA, ICWA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Adoption and Safe Families Act, Multi-Ethnic Placement Act, ICWA
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, tie comments to these landmark laws (e.g., ASFA, MEPA, Indian Child Welfare Act) to explain statutory consistency, conflicts, or implementation concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide state-level program impact data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include quantitative and qualitative data showing how the proposed rule would affect state programs (costs, caseloads, service availability), with citations to sources or state-level analyses where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address tribal consultation for ICWA-related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Address tribal consultation for Indian Child Welfare Act-related rules
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the NPRM implicates ICWA, describe tribal consultation that has occurred or should occur; note tribal perspectives, government-to-government considerations, and how tribal input affects implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with the Family First Prevention Services Act framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with Family First Prevention Services Act framework
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how the proposal aligns or conflicts with Family First requirements and implementation (prevention services, eligibility, funding, and placement considerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite prior federal guidance (IMs and PIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite federal IM (Information Memorandum) and PI (Program Instruction) prior guidance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference existing federal guidance documents (IMs, PIs) that interpret or implement statutes to show precedents, expectations, or administrative practices relevant to the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Children's Bureau performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference Children's Bureau performance metrics (CFSR, AFCARS)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground comments in established performance metrics such as the Child and Family Services Reviews (CFSR) and the Adoption and Foster Care Analysis and Reporting System (AFCARS) when addressing outcomes, compliance, or monitoring implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide data on outcomes (permanency, safety, well-being)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide data on outcomes (permanency, safety, well-being)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outcome measures (e.g., permanency rates, safety indicators, well-being metrics) to support assertions about likely effects of the rule; supply sources and methodologies for your data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with State plan/preprint requirements where applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with State plan/preprint requirements where applicable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rule affects State plans or preprint requirements, explain compliance implications, timing, and administrative burdens or benefits for State plan development and submission.
